label: Saree
description: The timeless garment draped 5.5 to 9 yards around the body. India's most iconic ethnic garment worn by women across all regions and occasions.

label: Salwar Suit
description: Three-piece ensemble comprising kameez (top), salwar (pants), and dupatta (scarf). The most versatile category of Indian women's wear spanning casual to formal.

label: Kurta
description: Collarless top of varying lengths worn over salwar, pants, leggings, or skirts. A staple of everyday Indian women's (and men's) fashion across all regions.

label: Dupatta
description: A long, versatile scarf worn across the chest or draped over the shoulders. Can transform a simple kurta into festival wear. Phulkari dupattas from Punjab and Bandhani from Rajasthan are regional specialties.

label: Lehenga Choli
description: A three-piece ensemble of flared skirt (lehenga), fitted blouse (choli), and dupatta. The most elaborate Indian occasion wear, especially for weddings. The chaniya choli version is quintessential Navratri Garba wear.

label: Palazzo Pants
description: Wide-leg, flowy pants that pair with kurtis, crop tops, and ethnic blouses. A modern Indian fashion staple that bridges ethnic and contemporary styles. Very comfortable for the Indian climate.

label: Anarkali
description: A long, flowy frock-style kurta inspired by Mughal court fashion, named after the legendary dancer Anarkali. The floor-length version creates a regal silhouette. Popular for weddings, festivals, and formal evening events.

label: Kurti
description: A shorter version of the kurta (typically above the knee), usually worn with jeans, leggings, or tights. India's most popular everyday garment for urban women — bridges ethnic and casual wear effortlessly.

label: Indo-Western
description: Contemporary fusion silhouettes blending Indian ethnic elements with Western fashion sensibilities. Popular among the urban professional and millennial demographic. Cape jackets with lehengas, saree gowns, and dhoti-pants with crop tops are key pieces.

label: Churidar
description: Fitted trousers that gather in horizontal folds below the knee, creating a 'bangle' effect at the ankle. More fitted than salwar, usually paired with long kurtas or anarkalis. A staple in South Indian fashion and popular across India.
